corrections.old: Pass through the parietal foramen, mastoid foramen, condylar canal, sphenoidal emissary foramen (of Vesalius), foramen ovale, foramen lacerum and foramen cecum
corrections.new: Pass through the parietal foramen, mastoid foramen, condylar canal, sphenoidal emissary foramen (of Vesalius), foramen ovale and foramen cecum
corrections.ref: Netter Plate 20 (p75): foramen lacerum transmits nothing (greater petrosal nerve passes over it); consistency with foramen-lacerum bone card

corrections.old: Drains the pterygoid plexus, linked to the cavernous sinus via emissary veins (foramen ovale, foramen lacerum), so facial/dental infection can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis; torn by displaced condylar neck fractures.
corrections.new: Drains the pterygoid plexus, linked to the cavernous sinus via emissary veins (foramen ovale, sphenoidal emissary foramen), so facial/dental infection can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis; torn by displaced condylar neck fractures.
corrections.ref: Netter Plate 20 (p75); consistency with foramen-lacerum, pterygoid-venous-plexus and cavernous-sinus cards
corrections.reason: Pearl cited a foramen lacerum emissary vein; the other vein cards and the bone card name the sphenoidal emissary foramen and foramen ovale

notes: All 37 vein cards checked: every "Drains into" has the matching tributary on the parent card (IJV, EJV, subclavian, brachiocephalic, facial/common facial, retromandibular, cavernous, transverse/sigmoid, confluence, straight sinus) and emissary routes match bone foramina. Only the foramen lacerum references conflict.
